title: Silent socket detection and token-reconciliation for streaming responses
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity spike on 2026-02-26 we observed a class of streaming failures where established streaming connections became silent for long periods and clients saw either truncated output (partial tokens) or indefinite stalls without clear disconnect events. This ticket tracks investigation findings, short-term mitigations, and durable fixes to avoid silent-socket stalls and to provide deterministic resume/reconciliation semantics for clients.
timeline: 2026-02-26 03:12 UTC: First customer alert — downstream clients report incomplete generations and stalled streams.
2026-02-26 03:25 UTC: On-call identified increased socket inactivity on a subset of frontend nodes while backend GPUs continued producing tokens.
2026-02-26 03:40 UTC: Emergency mitigation — temporarily disabled aggressive router batching for affected zones and enabled synchronous fallback to chunked polling for critical customers.
2026-02-26 04:10 UTC: Mitigation validated; customer-visible errors reduced but several sessions still experienced partial outputs.
2026-03-01: Postmortem kickoff and incremental telemetry added to capture last-seen-producer-offset per connection.
2026-03-10: Root-cause analysis completed — correlation between slow client reads, router buffer exhaustion, and mid-path proxy TCP stalls.
2026-03-14: Engineering started implementing server-side quiet-probe + token-sequence markers and test harness for slow-consumer simulations.
2026-03-21: Target date for first patch release with heartbeat probes and improved reconnect guidance.
2026-04-04: Target date for protocol changes and integration tests to land in runtime-1.19 release.
2026-04-18: Target date for dashboarding and alerts for silent-stream-rate regressions.
impact: Multiple enterprise customers reported truncated responses and requests that appeared to hang for >60s. Estimated affected sessions: 0.6% of streaming sessions during peak spike; major impact for low-latency streaming SLAs and interactive UIs.
root_cause: When a downstream client became slow reading the socket, intermediate router buffers (continuous batching + per-connection queues) could fill. A mid-path proxy TCP window scaling corner case allowed socket to remain established but with no progress on application-layer frames. The runtime continued producing tokens into the KV/cache path but the frontend did not surface completion events. Additionally, the streaming wire protocol lacked an explicit per-frame sequence marker that would allow clients to detect and request replay of missing tokens after reconnects.
mitigation: Short-term: (1) Disable aggressive batching for connections detected to have high write backlog, (2) make router emit early 429/503 when write queue exceeds threshold and route to non-streaming fallback, (3) add temporary monitoring to detect prolonged zero-byte reads >5s and alert.
action_items: (A1) Implement server-side quiet-probe (application heartbeat) that triggers after 2s of zero-byte writes to a connection. If probe elicits no progress, mark connection as candidate for graceful drift-recovery and attempt a resumed stream handshake. Owner: Diego Morales. Due: 2026-03-21.

(A2) Add per-frame monotonically-increasing sequence IDs and finalization markers to streaming frames so clients can reconcile partial tokens on reconnect. Owner: Runtime team (lead: Priya Nair). Due: 2026-04-04.

(A3) Harden router backpressure policy: introduce a soft-limit at which we reduce batching priority for the affected connection and a hard-limit that returns 503 to caller for new requests. Owner: Routing team (lead: Eric Huang). Due: 2026-03-18.

(A4) Build an integration test harness that simulates slow consumers, mid-path TCP stalls, and proxy window edge cases. Include CI scenarios that run at PR gating. Owner: SRE (lead: Marta Gomez). Due: 2026-03-28.
(A5) Dashboard and SLO alert: visible metric 'silent_stream_rate' and alert when >0.1% of streams per minute exceed 5s of inactivity. Owner: Observability team. Due: 2026-04-18.

(A6) Customer communication: prepare an incident FAQ and recommended client-side SDK guidance (auto-reconnect backoffs, idempotent resume tokens, and prefer polling fallback) and share with affected customers. Owner: Solutions Eng (lead: Ben Kramer). Due: 2026-03-16.

(A7) Post-deploy audit: run replay tests against production traffic snapshots to validate that per-frame sequence markers enable successful token reconciliation. Owner: Applied ML & Runtime QA. Due: 2026-04-08.

2026-03-10: Short-term router throttle patch deployed to canary cluster; observed 80% reduction in partial-output incidents for canary customers.
2026-03-12: Design review completed for per-frame sequence ID wire change; notes: conformance path for older clients required.

links: Design doc for per-frame sequence IDs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcSequenceDesign
notes: Decisions and trade-offs: We prefer adding sequence IDs and heartbeat probes over increasing TCP timeouts because the former gives application-level determinism and supports resume semantics across proxies and TCP restarts. Backwards compatibility: include a negotiated 'stream-v2' flag; older SDKs will fall back to existing behavior but will be guided to upgrade via Solutions Eng. Security: sequence IDs contain no customer data and are cryptographically random per-session to avoid correlation across users. Follow-up: consider batching-level instrumentation to better attribute cost regressions to per-customer throttling.
